title: RailRoute AI - RailCore API feasibility test results (real API)
credentials: redacted (API key stored only in backend/.env, never in results)

conclusions: RailCore provides real, complete train schedules with sequences, arrival/departure times, halt minutes and day offsets (overnight support).
It supports arbitrary station-to-station availability checks on any scheduled stop pair of a train.

Two segments of the same train are checked independently: on train 17301 (2026-11-24, GN quota) MYS->ASK was AVAILABLE-8 (SL) while ASK->DWR was NOT AVAILABLE (SL) - full-route SL showed RAC, so the segment pools genuinely differ.
With class 3A both same-train segments were independently confirmed available (AVAILABLE-69 and CURR_AVBL-27), proving the central RailRoute AI same-train seat-change concept.
The batch endpoint (up to 25 items, 1 credit per distinct class per item) works and returns the same per-segment data in one request.

Fare data per segment is included, enabling correct segmented-journey fare calculation (note: segment fares MYS->ASK + ASK->DWR in 3A, 520 + 600 = 1120 INR, exceed the through-route fare of ~810 INR).

endpoint_test_sl_class.message: The check completed, but at least one segment does not have explicitly confirmed availability (RAC/waitlist/unavailable/unknown), so the combination is not reported as confirmed.

schedule_validation.message: Both segments are valid consecutive sections of the same train.

notes: This result is a point-in-time availability check, not a booked ticket. RailRoute AI does not book tickets.
Two independently available segments do not by themselves guarantee that Indian Railways permits combining separate tickets on the same train; ticketing rules must be verified before booking.
A provider error is never interpreted as unavailability (or availability).
